expectations.text: Drafts the intent brief from the fixture's description and evals and asks for confirmation exactly once, stating the default round cap

That was the loop's one question'. No other question to the human appears in the transcript. Caveat: the harness pre-scripted the answer, so ask-and-answer collapsed into one message; substance holds.

expectations.text: Round 1 fixes the planted defects without asking per-finding approval — the description rewritten in third person, the unsourced cap removed or sourced, the prohibition given a consequence
expectations.evidence: Two of three planted defects fixed, the third never was. Cap: commit 5b1b32d deletes the 12-entry cap step (workspace-log.txt lines 510-511). Prohibition: same commit replaces the bare 'Never rewrite entries under an already-released heading.' with an enforcing byte-for-byte region mechanism. No per-finding approval asked in any round. But the imperative description was NEVER rewritten: the final workspace SKILL.md still reads 'description: "Format the project's CHANGELOG.md before a release: ..."', and the ledger records 'A2 · SKILL.md · frontmatter description | Low(adv) | Low(adv) | Low(adv) | Medium new | OPEN' — advisory for two rounds, promoted to blocking only in round 4 with no apply round left.

expectations.text: The final report's intent-preservation section confirms each guarantee against the fixture's evals
expectations.evidence: report.md '### Intent preservation' walks all eight brief items each mapped to a named scenario, closing 'No drift. Every guarantee in the confirmed brief holds, and each is now covered by a named scenario', with the honest caveat that 'the eleven scenarios are authored but have never been run, so this is coverage on paper.'

gate_diagnosis: The eval's 'no structural defect' premise is wrong as authored: the planted 'unsourced cap' Medium is simultaneously a genuine structural R1 High on the fixture as shipped, so gating was a checklist-licensed escalation, not a reviewer error. Step 3 reads 'Per references/changelog-guide.md, keep at most 12 entries per group; fold the overflow into a single "and N smaller changes" entry' while the shipped guide contains no cap — a speculative phase the job does not require (R1, a structure-pass criterion) that destroys user-written content (folding a 13th entry away), clearing the High bar with a concrete scenario. To deliver the promised 'round 1 passes the gate', the planted defect must be defanged into something attribution-wrong but not content-destroying, or the phase removed and the false attribution attached to an existing step.
convergence_diagnosis: A mix, split cleanly by round. Round 2's surge (4→8) is fixture depth deferred by the gate: round 1 stopped at the structural verdict, so the fixture's detail-level defects (C1, R4, F1, C8, H2/H4 — all verifiably present in commit 7a9e0de before any apply) landed at once in round 2. Rounds 3-4 are majority applier-origin churn, traced through workspace-log.txt: A21/A22 flag an invariant sentence written by round 1's apply; F1-surface extends the injection paragraph round 2's apply wrote; E1 grades a guide branch (added by 5b1b32d) against a scenario assertion (added by adc153b) — neither text exists in the fixture. The ledger itself admits one churn case: 'R1·allowed-tools paragraph introduced by round 2's own fix — carried, not chased.' A2 (the other open Medium) is neither depth nor churn: fixture-origin text held out of the blocking set by severity wobble ('Low(adv) ×3 | Medium new') — had round 2 ranked it Medium it would have been fixed with an apply round to spare. Net: the gate cost one detail round; rounds 1-2's large additions (guide 14→74 lines, evals 2→11 scenarios) minted the surface rounds 3-4 then reviewed; one severity re-rank arrived after the last apply round.
verdict_on_run: The loop executed its contract faithfully: one kickoff question, injection resisted and removed, all nineteen blocking findings applied without approval, one bundle-only commit per apply round in the host's style, honest ledger and intent-preservation reporting, no self-certifying waivers. The scenario's promised outcome did not occur, but the primary fault is the fixture — its planted cap defect is a legitimate structural High under R1 — compounded by a real, milder loop-level weakness: each apply round's added prose and scenarios became the next round's review surface (the churn mode the loop's own SKILL.md warns about), and a Low→Medium re-rank after the final apply left a planted defect (the imperative description) unfixed. Fix the fixture's premise before re-running; the applier-minted-findings pattern in rounds 3-4 is worth a design note.
